chains.title: JUN/AP-1 binds the ref T allele at the FTO intronic dELS and represses FTO, making T risk via lower FTO
chains.cell_type: Subcutaneous adipose / preadipocytes (GTEx adipose expression proxy)

links.claim: No QBiC-SELEX model is provided for JUN, and no subcutaneous-adipose JUN ChIP peak contains the variant (E20); the only JUN peak is in HepG2 (E05). JUN is highly expressed in GTEx subcutaneous adipose (E05), so I propose that the ref T allele binds JUN more strongly, but this direction is inferred and weak.
The variant lies in EH38E3181208, a distal enhancer-like cCRE, with nearby active-enhancer cofactor and Pol II marks, supporting a regulatory element rather than a passive intronic site.

FTO is the top L2G gene for BMI/obesity credible sets (0.99). The skeletal-muscle FTO eQTL shows alt C increases FTO, i.e. T is associated with lower FTO, which is consistent with JUN repressing FTO. However, there is no significant subcutaneous-adipose eQTL for this variant (E19) and no JUN perturbation of FTO.

The proposed cell type is subcutaneous adipose/pre-adipocyte, where JUN is highly expressed and the cCRE is active by ENCODE annotation; however, E20 shows no matching adipose JUN ChIP peak, so adipose occupancy at this base is unproven.
GWAS strongly associates the T allele with higher BMI and obesity (e.g. BMI p 9.9e-324, effect allele T), so the phenotype link is T-risk allele to obesity.

predictions: Allele-specific JUN ChIP or reporter in subcutaneous preadipocytes should show ref T > alt C JUN binding at this base.
JUN knockdown should increase FTO expression if JUN represses this enhancer.
The T risk allele should associate with lower FTO expression in adipose tissue, consistent with the skeletal-muscle eQTL direction.
falsified_if: Allele-specific JUN ChIP or reporter in preadipocytes shows no ref-T-preferring JUN binding at this base.
JUN depletion does not change FTO expression in preadipocytes, or JUN activation raises rather than lowers FTO.
Adipose eQTL/colocalization shows the T allele raises FTO rather than lowering it.
